record.context_brief: Chaos on singular parts of integrable systems
record.original_question: For an integrable system on a compact 2n-dimensional manifold with n independent commuting first integrals almost everywhere, how wild can the dynamics be on singular submanifolds where the integrals become dependent? What constraints does integrability impose, and can chaotic behavior occur on a tiny singular submanifold?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M^{2n}, \omega)$ be a compact symplectic manifold of dimension $2n$ equipped with $n$ smooth functions $f_1, \dots, f_n : M \to \mathbb{R}$ that pairwise Poisson-commute, $\{f_i, f_j\} = 0$ for all $i, j$, and whose differentials $df_1, \dots, df_n$ are linearly independent on an open dense subset $U \subset M$. Let $X_{f_1}$ be the Hamiltonian vector field of $f_1$, and let $S := M \setminus U$ denote the singular set where the integrals fail to be independent.

(a) Describe the possible dynamical behaviors of $X_{f_1}$ restricted to invariant subsets of the singular submanifold $S$. In particular, determine what constraints (if any) are imposed by the existence of the commuting integrals on $M$.

(b) Decide whether the flow of $X_{f_1}$ on $S$ (or on an invariant subset of $S$) can exhibit chaotic behavior — for instance, positive topological entropy, a horseshoe, or sensitive dependence on initial conditions — even when $S$ is arbitrarily small (e.g., of arbitrarily small Hausdorff dimension or measure) inside $M$.

(c) Construct an example, or prove the impossibility of such, of a smooth integrable system in the above sense whose restriction to the singular set $S$ supports topologically chaotic dynamics while the integrability on $M \setminus S$ is preserved.
artifact.status_search_result: The question concerns the dynamics of integrable Hamiltonian systems on their singular sets, an active research area at the interface of integrable systems and singularity theory. Recent surveys and problem lists on finite-dimensional integrable systems list questions about singular fibers and chaos on them as open, and no general classification or example resolving the question appears in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems, Questions, and Challenges in Finite-Dimensional Integrable Systems
status_evidence.snippet: List of open problems on singularities and dynamics in finite-dimensional integrable Hamiltonian systems.
status_evidence.claim: Problems regarding the structure of singular fibers and dynamics on them are listed as open in recent surveys.

status_evidence.title: Integrable Hamiltonian Systems and Singularities
status_evidence.snippet: Researchers have discerned clear boundaries between integrable behaviour and chaotic dynamics, thus shedding light on the delicate interplay of integrals of motion and singularity formations.
status_evidence.claim: The interplay between integrability and chaotic behavior near singularities remains an active research topic.
